The SOME/IP Transformer shall only provide functions for transformers where the TransformationTechnology is referenced as the first ref- erence in the list of ordered references transformer from a DataTransformation to a TransformationTechnology .

The SOME/IP transformer defined in this document shall be used as a transformer if • the attribute protocol of the TransformationTechnology is set to SOMEIP • and the attribute version of the TransformationTechnology is set to 1 • and the attribute transformerClass of the TransformationTechnology is set to serializer

For interoperability reasons the header layout shall be iden- tical for all implementations of SOME/IP and is described as follows: 1. Message ID (Service ID / Method ID) [32 bit] 2. Length [32 bit] 3. Additional information: (a) Protocol Version [8 bit] (b) Interface Version [8 bit] (c) Message Type [8 bit] (d) Return Code [8 bit] 4. Payload [variable size…
The Request ID field shall be 32 bit long.
The Protocol Version field shall be 8 bit long.
The Protocol Version field shall contain the SOME/IP pro- tocol version.
The Interface Version field shall contain the Version of the Service Interface.
The Message Type field shall be 8 bit long.
The Return Code field shall be 8 bit long.
The Return Code field shall be used to signal whether a request has been successfully processed.
The Payload field shall have variable size.
The Payload field shall contain the transported data.
The allowed Return Codes for specific message types are specified in Table 7.7.
To allow migration the deserialization shall ignore parame- ters attached to the end of previously known parameter list.
In case of Client/Server communication the Return Code shall transport the ApplicationError s of the executed ClientServerOperation if no SOME/IP error occurred.
The byte order of the parameters inside the payload shall be defined by byteOrder of SOMEIPTransformationDescription .
The payload of a message for Sender/Receiver communi- cation shall consists of the serialized data element that is transported.
